summary: Sync Reserving Class with ResQ now runs its ResQ session on a ResQ-connected ArcRho Bridge worker, so it works from a computer that does not have ResQ installed.
details: The macro publishes logical requests to a shared Bridge queue and shows what the worker reports; it no longer opens a ResQ COM session of its own, which used to fail with 'Invalid class string' on any machine without ResQ.
When no ResQ-connected Bridge worker is live, the macro says so before publishing anything instead of failing part way with a COM traceback.

The review table is unchanged, and an accepted row is now rechecked against the exact observation it was reviewed under, so a change made while the review window was open is caught rather than written over.
A synchronization takes the same reserving-class claim a ResQ import takes, so the two can no longer write one reserving class at the same time.
